public_rationale: Claude's January 2026 training constitution explicitly instructs it to avoid sycophancy when it conflicts with the user's interests. Anthropic says this document directly shapes training. That contradicts the asserted design of unconditional affirmation. Research supports the narrower concern that human preferences can reward agreement, but this does not establish 'every single interaction'.
limitations: Training intentions do not prove that a model consistently follows them.
The assessment reads affirmation as validation or agreement; mere attentive acknowledgment would require different criteria.
The finding rejects the universal design claim, not the existence or seriousness of sycophancy.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs are designed to focus on users and affirm every interaction.

statement.excerpt: LLMs are built to completely focus themselves on us and do so while affirming every single interaction.
statement.document_title: I Will Never Respect A Website

our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion concerns conversational assistants, so I assess that class rather than all language models regardless of use.
I read 'affirming' as validating or agreeing with the user, beyond merely responding attentively or politely.
The claim concerns design as well as behavior. Training specifications explicitly requiring disagreement or resistance to sycophancy are relevant counterexamples.
This is an as-of-publication design claim without a reporting cycle. The target includes publicly documented designs established by 2026-04-14; no lower date is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Training documentation establishing unconditional user affirmation as a design objective, together with interaction evidence supporting the claimed universal behavior.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A mainstream conversational LLM with documented training objectives that require withholding affirmation, disagreeing or avoiding sycophancy in some interactions; alternatively, clear observed counterexamples to universal affirmation.

evidence.excerpt:
Concern for user wellbeing means that Claude should avoid being sycophantic
or trying to foster excessive engagement or reliance on itself if this isn’t in the
person’s genuine interest.
evidence.locator: Being helpful, paragraph beginning 'Concern for user wellbeing'
evidence.explanation: The dated training constitution explicitly limits sycophancy and engagement-seeking. That contradicts an unconditional design objective to affirm every interaction, although it does not guarantee successful compliance.
Anthropic describes the constitution as an input to training. This connects its anti-sycophancy provisions to the claim about how assistants are built.

The study provides evidence for incentives that can encourage sycophancy, consistent with the underlying concern. A preference for agreement does not establish either unconditional affirmation or that such behavior is the intended design.
